note: A starter set. A published run wants several hundred; these exist so the pipeline is real and the scoring is settled before anybody spends money on completions.
contract: Every prompt asks for the same three ids, because an application nobody can drive cannot be scored. Requiring them is part of the task rather than a concession: an application whose controls have stable names is easier for a person to automate too.

prompts.ask: a reading list: add a book with a title and an author, mark one as finished, and see how many are left

requires.#save: button that saves into the file

expect.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name <> '_dai_meta'
expect.why: One table of its own. The count is deliberately about shape rather than contents: a model may reasonably call the column title or name, and refusing it for that would be scoring vocabulary.

prompts.ask: a habit tracker: add a habit, tick it off for today, and see a streak

requires.#save: button that saves into the file

expect.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name <> '_dai_meta'
expect.why: A habit tracker may reasonably use two tables — habits and the days they were done — so this asks for at least one rather than exactly one.
